title: August and the Wolf
premise: Casper Blackwood, a memory-thief hiding in the magic-outlawed city of Vell, has spent twelve years selling stolen recollections as charms while concealing their own erased past. When the old gods resume answering prayers, Casper discovers they are the last living anchor of the covenant between mortal and divine realms—and that the usurper King Aldric means to sever it forever and claim godhood himself. Hunted by Aldric's witch-finders and shadowed by Wren, a wolf-god's exiled huntress who remembers Casper better than Casper remembers themselves, they journey to the shattered Godstone to reforge the covenant. In the end, Casper must sacrifice their recovered memories—the last twelve years of love and survival—to seal the covenant anew, choosing duty over self even as Wren vows to remember them for both.
about_author: I. M. Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in coastal libraries before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about memory, debt, and the small magics people trade away to survive.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hour
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In the night market of Vell, Casper sells a widow a charm woven from her late husband's happiest hour—then quietly steals a memory from a drunk soldier to restock their wares. The beat establishes Casper's moral compromise and loneliness: they are skilled at giving others back what they themselves have lost.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A child's desperate prayer at a shuttered shrine is answered—a candle relights itself, and the old gods stir citywide. Witch-finders sweep the streets. Casper feels the covenant's broken threads tugging at something buried inside them, and for the first time in twelve years, they are afraid of being found.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, huntress of the exiled wolf-god Fenmarrow, tracks the 'anchor' her dying god spoke of and finds Casper. She knows their face, their name, their laugh—things Casper cannot recall ever owning. The beat is uncanny intimacy: being loved by a stranger who insists she isn't one.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Edict
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. King Aldric declares all god-touched persons forfeit; his armies march on the free cities. Casper learns from a dying fence that their erased memories were payment—they once brokered the original covenant and paid with themselves. Wren offers escape north; Casper chooses instead to run toward the truth.

chapters.title: Salt Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Fleeing along the coast ahead of witch-finders, Wren and Casper shelter in a drowned chapel where Fenmarrow's fading voice speaks through tide-pools. Wren wrestles with duty to her god versus her growing tenderness for someone who may not survive remembering. First kiss, immediately interrupted by hunters.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Captured by the witch-finder Serah Vole, Casper bargains with stolen memories, revealing fragments of their past: a younger Casper kneeling before the Godstone, swearing an oath. Vole lets them go—not mercy, but a trap, marked so Aldric can follow them to the covenant's heart.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Free Cities
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They reach the free cities just as Aldric's vanguard burns the outlying towns; refugees carry prayers the gods can no longer answer. Casper sees the cost of their invisibility made flesh. The emotional beat is guilt hardening into resolve: no more hiding, whatever the price.

chapters.title: The Godstone
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the shattered Godstone, Fenmarrow spends his last strength to show Casper the whole truth: they were the covenant's first oath-keeper, and only willing sacrifice—one life's memories entire—can reforge it. Wren begs Casper to refuse. Casper, finally whole in memory, says yes anyway.

chapters.title: Aldric Ascendant
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Aldric arrives to seize godhood at the moment of reforging; battle erupts between his witch-finders and Fenmarrow's last pack. Wren holds the line, wounded, while Casper walks the burning stone. The climax: Casper speaks the old oath and begins pouring away every memory—Vell, the thefts, Wren—into the covenant.

chapters.title: August, Again
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The covenant seals; the gods return; Aldric, half-divine and unclaimed by any god, crumbles. Casper survives but empty, a stranger in their own skin, sitting in an August field. Wren sits beside them and begins, gently, to tell them everything—vowing to be their memory until love writes new ones. Quiet, hopeful resolution.
